label: About
title: About The Canopy Comes Apart
short_blurb: A daily generated front page where the image is the interface.
body: Daily Frontpage is a daily generated interactive front page. Each edition starts from recent saved signals and source research, becomes a new image-led scene, and stays explorable in the archive. The image is the interface: visible marks, objects, and surfaces in the scene open the real sources that shaped the day.

This iteration began with 1216 recent saved-signal files and 949 captured links, then narrowed the page to 9 source windows around @HeavyMetalInk: Hiroo Isono (1945–2013) was a Japanese illustrator known for his dreamlike... and NTS liked tracks source map, plus 7 more. A source image from pbs.twimg.com helped set the palette, contrast, edge behavior, and gesture. The scene became The Canopy Comes Apart: Nocturnal botanical torn poster wall, near-frontal close view with slight lateral parallax and shallow lifted-edge shadows, no surround. Split stippled emerald forest into three unequal print masses around an off-center black basin; crop a peach-rimmed giant crown through upper left. After the image was made, a plate-reading pass mapped 9 visible regions and the mask audit tightened them against Peach-lit scalloped outer canopy edge, Lower-left scalloped leaf overlap, and Dark notch beneath a green leaf.

typography.rationale: Bricolage Grotesque and Space Grotesk fit record, arcade, and listening-room editions while Fraunces keeps source captions tactile.
